plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value minus a small amount. This is because bidding too high risks overpaying, while bidding too low risks losing the item even when it's worth more than the bid. Since this is round 1 and there is no previous history, I will bid slightly below my value to attempt to win at a reasonable price. I will bid $24.5.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $49, a reasonable expectation for the second highest bid is around half of my value. To avoid losing to a slightly higher bid, I will bid a small increment above that. My value is $31, so I'll bid around $15.5 + a small amount.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any bid below your value risks losing the auction for an item you'd be happy to win, and any bid above your value risks winning the auction and paying more than the item is worth to you. Since this is round 1 and there's no history, I will bid my true value.
